bullets.text: CR was 92.6, exceeding target profitability; net income was just short of $1.2B; 2008 margins are expected to more closely approximate the 96 CR goal.
Recapitalization returned ~$3B via share repurchases and a $2/share extraordinary dividend; issued $1B hybrid debt; debt-to-capital was 30.6%; portfolio total return 4.7%.
Written and earned premiums fell short of 2006 by 3% and 2%, respectively; rate decreases were not fully offset by policy increases; industry written premiums estimated flat.
Ended 2007 with more customers than any prior year; personal auto PIF +2% (Direct +7%, Agency -1%); Special Lines +8%; Commercial Auto +7%.

Believes pricing is almost fully adjusted to reflect favorable frequency; rates and losses appear more in balance; expects higher likelihood of rate increases to match claims inflation, primarily bodily injury.

Claims cost inflation is primarily driven by bodily injury severities, contrasting with 1.5 years of rate cuts; multi-year Claims investments are producing high-quality resolutions, better customer experiences, and productivity advances.

Consolidated into a centralized marketing group under a single Progressive brand; Immediate Response Vehicle re-established as icon; secured Cleveland Indians ballpark naming rights for Progressive Field.
Expense ratio rose to 21.1 from 20.2 in 2006, deleveraged by falling average premium per policy; organizational changes made to lower non-claims expenses.
First customers using wireless vehicle-activity data for usage-based insurance; expanded e-signature, e-fulfillment, and paperless self-service; rated #1 auto insurance site by Keynote.
Sub-prime direct exposure was under 2% of the portfolio; market value of bond and preferred holdings in large financial institutions declined; net unrealized portfolio gains ended at $715.4M.
